title: Comparison of methanol and isopropanol as wash solvents for determination of hair cortisol concentration in grizzly bears and polar bears
author: Kroshko, Kapronczai, et al.

steps.title: Collect guard hair samples
steps.instruction: From each bear, collect 16 guard hair samples each weighing approximately 50 mg, selecting hairs that are visually similar, similarly contaminated, and from the same body location.

steps.title: Assign samples to solvents
steps.instruction: Divide the 16 samples per bear into two groups of eight: one group for methanol wash dynamics and the other for isopropanol wash dynamics.

steps.title: Perform sequential solvent washes
steps.instruction: For each sample, carry out a series of wash cycles ranging from one to eight washes. In each wash cycle, mix the hair with 2.0 ml of the assigned solvent (methanol or isopropanol) on a slow rotator for 3 min, then remove the hair and dry it thoroughly before the next cycle.

substeps.instruction: Place hair in a tube with 2.0 ml solvent.
Repeat the above steps for the required number of washes (1‑8).

steps.title: Grind washed hair to powder
steps.instruction: Using a Retsch MM 301 Mixer Mill, grind the washed hair into a fine powder.

steps.title: Extract cortisol from hair powder
steps.instruction: Weigh 25 mg of the powdered hair, incubate it on a slow rotator for 12 h with 0.5 ml methanol, then centrifuge the mixture for 15 min at 2150 g.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.5 ml methanol to 25 mg powder.

steps.title: Evaporate and reconstitute extracts
steps.instruction: Evaporate the supernatant methanol at 38 °C under a stream of nitrogen gas; reconstitute the dried residue in 0.2 ml phosphate assay diluent buffer (provided with the ELISA kit).

steps.title: Prepare wash‑solvent extracts
steps.instruction: Take the final wash solvent from each sample, evaporate it under nitrogen, and reconstitute the residue in 0.4 ml assay diluent buffer.

steps.title: Quantify cortisol by ELISA (EA65)
steps.instruction: Measure cortisol in both the hair‑extract and the wash‑solvent reconstitutions using the Oxford Biomedical ELISA kit (catalogue EA65, Lansing, MI) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Record assay performance characteristics
steps.instruction: Note the following ELISA performance data: intra‑assay %CV = 3.58–9.74 %, inter‑assay %CV = 5.75–11.44 %; extraction efficiencies = 94.2 ± 5.1 % (grizzly) and 95.6 ± 3.2 % (polar); limit of detection = 0.04 ng ml⁻¹ (equivalent to 0.32 pg cortisol mg⁻¹ hair for a 25 mg sample).

steps.title: Compare ELISA kits
steps.instruction: Use seven 50 mg hair samples (four grizzly, three polar). Perform three wash cycles with either methanol or isopropanol as described above, then grind, extract, dry, and reconstitute each sample in the assay diluent buffer supplied with each kit. Run cortisol assays with four kits: Oxford EA65 (catalogue EA65), Salimetrics salivary cortisol ELISA (catalogue 1‑3002), Cayman cortisol ELISA (catalogue 500360), and the modified Oxford EA65 kit (new primary antibody, 2016).

substeps.instruction: Apply three wash cycles to each sample.
Grind and extract as in steps 4‑6.
Run ELISA with each of the four kits.
